figures.caption: Table 1. Overview of PBN variants. The first 4 variants progressively introduce local predictive objectives andlocal learning, culminating in PBN local gradients (as our main fully PC-compliant condition). The last 2variants retain all six PC requirements while adopting increasingly classic PC implementations through explicitprior subtraction and, in PBN classic PC, invariance-based learning without augmentations.

Figure 3. Unique variance explained by the decoder in brain data, excluding encoder-explainedvariance. Main: Noise-ceiling-corrected unique variance (R²) explained by the PBN decoder in human fMRIresponses, after factoring out variance explained by the encoder, for naturalistic images from (Allen et al., 2022) NSD 515 shared images. Bars show the mean across subjects for each model variant and brain region;error bars indicate 95% confidence intervals. Top right: Venn diagram illustrating the partition of uniquedecoder-explained variance (green) and the variance partitions factored out as encoder-explained variance(red).

Table 2. Downstream performance accuracy on the UCF-101 dataset and the Moments in Time test set. Allcells show mean accuracy ± standard deviation across 5-fold cross-validation splits. Best performing modelshown in bold. Established networks perform best, while PBN backprop, PBN backprop + local loss, and PBNbackprop local gradients consistently outperform PredNet and perform closer to the performance of theestablished models.

Figure 6. Visualization of PBN model variants. Top left: PBN backprop, Top center: PBN backprop + localloss, Top right: PBN local gradients, Bottom left: PBN local gradients + subtract, Bottom right: PBN classicPC. Legend: CGC: Continuous Gated Cell. Simple residual recurrent cell with a gated residual state. (⟚): Stopgradients. At this location, gradients are prohibited from passing.

Figure 11. Layerwise model-brain similarity. Layerwise noise-corrected model-brain representationalsimilarity, as a response to the Natural Scenes Dataset (Allen et al., 2022), dissolved over model activationsand brain regions. Top left: PBN local gradients, Top right: ConvNeXt, Bottom left: ResNet-50, Bottomright: PredNet.

Figure 12. Prediction examples. Prediction examples for the PBN local gradients model variant. Left:Example input series from the test dataset. Center: Corresponding model predictions from the lowest-leveldecoder layer. Right: Model-inferred spatial uncertainty estimated using Monte Carlo dropout.Reconstructions are generally coarse, as pixel-perfect reconstruction is not the primary modeling objective(see Methods).
